entities.summary:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) is Nigeria's current ruling party, formed in 2013 from the merger of four opposition parties to defeat the incumbent People's Democratic Party (PDP), which had governed Nigeria since 1999. Muhammadu Buhari's 2015 victory under the APC banner was the first time an opposition party peacefully defeated a ruling party and transferred power in Nigeria's history.

The APC was created through the merger of the All Nigeria Peoples Party (ANPP), Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN), Congress for Progressive Change (CPC), and a faction of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA). The merger was motivated by the principle that only a unified opposition could defeat the PDP's 16-year hold on power, creating a broad political coalition with support from North, Southwest, and Southeast Nigeria.

Buhari's 2015 election victory on anti-corruption and security platforms marked a turning point in Nigerian democracy. However, his administration struggled with the Boko Haram insurgency, the rise of banditry in the Northwest, and an economic recession (2016). Bola Tinubu's 2023 election as APC candidate — controversial due to his political machine's dominance and questions about his age and qualifications — continued APC's hold on power, though with the weakest electoral showing in the party's history. Nigeria's 2023 elections saw a credibility crisis over election management.
